transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-29
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Marcus Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Ethan Park (CTO, Solace), Maya Alvarez (Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (SRE)

[00:00] Marcus Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda, want to run through your latency and throughput goals, current infra, and then Priya will go into the benchmarking options and hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs. Sound good?

[00:15] Ethan Park: Yeah thanks Marcus. Quick context, we run fraud-detect models and customer-facing nlp for real-time decisions. p95 latency is our primary SLA, we say 150ms p95 for single-turn generation, and for streaming chat responses we want tokens flowing within 50ms of initial response and stay under 300ms behind for subsequent tokens.

[00:36] Priya Rao: Got it, thanks. When you say 150ms p95 are you measuring end-to-end including network, or just inference?

[00:42] Maya Alvarez: We measure from our API gateway to response, so includes network. Our target for inference-only would be roughly 80-100ms p95 for the model. We expect additional 30-50ms overhead for routing.

[00:55] Marcus Chen: Good — so for sizing we need p95 inference and concurrency. What's your typical concurrency or QPS?

[01:02] Liam O'Connor: Peak concurrency about 250 concurrent requests during business hours. Average is 40 qps. Each request is usually 150-200 tokens prompt, and generation length varies 20-60 tokens. Streaming is enabled for UI.

[01:18] Priya Rao: Ok that's helpful. For 250 concurrent requests with streams, we usually recommend dedicated capacity for predictable p95, but hosted can work for initial evaluation. The main tradeoff is burstiness and tail latencies during noisy neighbor events on shared hosts.

[01:33] Ethan Park: Can you give a concrete token/sec / GPU mapping? We need to know how many GPUs to reserve if we go dedicated.

[01:40] Priya Rao: Sure, rough back-of-envelope: on A100-class or similar, for a 7B-ish model in FP16 you might see 500-800 tokens/sec when fully batched; with 13B it's more like 200-400 tokens/sec depending on quant and beam/temperature. But streaming and low-latency SLOs reduce effective throughput because batch windows have to be short. We can run customer-specific benchmarks to get exact token/sec numbers with your prompt mix.

[02:05] Maya Alvarez: Our prompts are high variability; some are short 40 tokens, others 200. We care about p95 single-turn and also about cold-starts when KV cache is empty. Any suggestions on caching?

[02:18] Priya Rao: We support automatic KV prefix caching for repeated prompts or similar prefixes. That reduces p95 significantly for follow-up calls. For cold-starts, dedicated with warmed model instances helps. Also quantization profiles can change single-token latency; per-model tuning during POC is key.

[02:36] Marcus Chen: We're hearing that you might start hosted POC then move to Dedicated for production. Any compliance constraints pushing to Private?

[02:43] Ethan Park: Data residency and audit trails are important. We have EU customers and banking clients; SOC2 is required, and we need keys managed in our KMS eventually. For pilot we'll anonymize data, but production needs VPC or on-prem options.

[02:58] Marcus Chen: Redwood Private supports VPC and bring-your-own-KMS, we can provide our security pack. We'll share SOC2 and deployment docs.

[03:05] Liam O'Connor: For networking, we'll need peering info and firewall rules. Also, what's your observed p95 for streaming token latency? Some vendors are 20-40ms first-byte but later tokens lag.

[03:18] Priya Rao: Streaming first-byte is typically bounded by model startup and token decode — we aim for sub-100ms first-byte on warmed instances; subsequent tokens are usually <30-50ms apart on optimized runtimes, but that depends on sequence length and batch effects. We'll validate with your prompt set.

[03:38] Ethan Park: For the benchmark, we'll want to run both hosted and dedicated to compare. Can Redwood spin up identical model versions in both modes? Also, how do you handle automatic failover if dedicated capacity is exhausted?

[03:50] Priya Rao: Yes same model versioning. For failover we support routing policies — can failover to a smaller variant or hosted pool; that's configurable. For a strict p95 SLA you'd pin to dedicated and configure burst/fallback policies.

[04:05] Maya Alvarez: What about token accounting? We need to estimate cost per million tokens for the different setups.

[04:10] Marcus Chen: We'll include cost SKU in the pricing deck. Generally hosted has per-token pricing, Dedicated is reserved capacity plus lower unit cost; Private has licensing and infra. We'll send a breakout.

[04:22] Priya Rao: Technical detail: for token/sec benchmarks we recommend a harness that replays your prompt distribution with realistic concurrency and inter-arrival times, measures p50/p95/p99, streaming first-byte, average token/sec, and GPU utilization. We'll provide the harness and can run a shared benchmark in our sandbox or give you the harness to run in your infra.

[04:45] Liam O'Connor: We prefer you run hosted POC because we don't want to spin infra for initial tests. Can you set up a dedicated sandbox environment with isolated pool?

[04:53] Priya Rao: We can provision a dedicated sandbox for the POC. For hosted POC we can also give a reserved quota to reduce noisy neighbor risk. Either way we'll make sure logging/tracing is enabled so we can map latencies to infra metrics.

[05:08] Ethan Park: On security, we need syslog / audit logs and SSO integration. Do you support SAML SSO and RBAC at the route level?

[05:15] Marcus Chen: Yes SAML/SSO supported, RBAC in the console, and audit logs with retention options. We'll include those details in the security doc.

[05:25] Maya Alvarez: For the POC success criteria: 80-100ms inference p95, end-to-end p95 <150ms, streaming first-byte <100ms, ability to sustain 250 concurrent sessions with 95% of requests meeting p95. Also cost per 1M tokens target under a threshold we'll share.

[05:45] Priya Rao: Noted. We'll tailor the benchmark to those success criteria and include model/quantization variants to explore cost-performance tradeoffs.

[05:56] Ethan Park: A couple of nitty-gritty: do you have examples of customers in fintech with similar p95 targets? Any public benchmarks?

[06:04] Marcus Chen: We have references and internal benchmarks; we'll share sanitized benchmark slides. We also have a short case study of a payments customer that hit similar p95s after moving to dedicated and enabling KV cache.

[06:20] Liam O'Connor: Operationally, if we go dedicated, how do updates and rollouts work? We need canary deploys and quick rollback capability.

[06:28] Priya Rao: Our rollout system supports canary, A/B, and instant rollback to previous pinned versions. You get per-route dashboards and traces to validate before full rollouts.

[06:40] Ethan Park: For the POC we'll need a timeline. What's realistic?

[06:44] Marcus Chen: Typical timeline: initial hosted benchmark within 1 week after we get sample prompts and test accounts, dedicated sandbox spin-up 1-2 weeks, full POC 2-4 weeks depending on scope.

[06:56] Maya Alvarez: That works. We'll try to get the sample prompts and firewall details by Friday.

[07:01] Marcus Chen: Great. I'll recap next steps.

[07:04] Marcus Chen: Action items: Marcus to send pricing + security docs; Priya to schedule benchmark and share harness; Maya to send prompts; Liam to share networking details. We'll aim to have the hosted benchmark run next Tues/Wed, and a follow-up to review results on Monday 2026-05-04.

[07:22] Ethan Park: Sounds good. Thanks everybody.

[07:26] Marcus Chen: Thanks. End call.
